TAKEAWAYS
Operating EBITDA margin
-- 30.1% for the full fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, a 40 basis point expansion, including a 180 basis point increase in the Legacy Business, achieved despite a 140 basis point headwind from Healthcare Solutions integration and tax credit expiry.
Collection and disposal EBITDA
-- Grew more than 8% in Q4, with margin expanding 160 basis points, driven by cost efficiencies and automation investments.
Operating expenses as a percentage of revenue
-- Improved sequentially each quarter to finish the year at 59.5%, marking the first time annual operating expenses were below 60% companywide.
SG&A ratio (Legacy Business)
-- 9.2% of revenue for the year, a 10 basis point improvement, while total company SG&A closed at 10.4%, reflecting ongoing cost rationalization.
Healthcare Solutions SG&A
-- Reached 20.8% in Q4, improving 350 basis points year over year, and was 10.4% for the company as a whole in 2025, signaling structural alignment progress.
Cash from operations
-- Increased over 12% to $6.04 billion for fiscal 2025.
Free cash flow
-- Rose nearly 27% to $2.94 billion, underpinned by higher margins and disciplined capital deployment.
Capital expenditures
-- Totaled just under $2.6 billion for maintenance and $633 million for sustainability growth in 2025; 2026 capex guidance is $2.65 billion to $2.75 billion, with about $200 million for high-return sustainability projects.
Dividend and capital returns
-- Board approved a 14.5% quarterly dividend increase for 2026 (23rd consecutive annual raise); $3.5 billion in planned returns through dividends and buybacks, representing over 90% of projected free cash flow.
Share repurchase program
-- $3 billion newly authorized for 2026.
Leverage ratio
-- Ended 2025 at 3.1x; targeting a range of 2.5x-3x for 2026.
Operating EBITDA 2026 guidance
-- $8.15 billion to $8.25 billion, excluding about $150 million of projected accretion expense to improve peer comparability.
Free cash flow 2026 outlook
-- Targeting nearly 30% growth to $3.8 billion at the midpoint, with operating EBITDA-to-free-cash-flow conversion rate above 46%.
Pricing
-- Core price of 6.2% achieved in Q4 for collection and disposal; 2026 core price guidance for collection and disposal at 5.6%.
Healthcare Solutions price and volume outlook
-- 2026 price expected at 4.2%; total top-line growth forecast at 3%, with lost account impact expected to diminish in the back half of the year.
Residential volume
-- Negative trend moderated in Q4; management expects improvement through 2026 and margin acceleration above 20% for residential in Q4.
EBITDA margin expansion (2026)
-- Guided for 30 basis points of expansion at midpoint; adjusted for wildfire impact, 50 basis points underlying expansion expected, led by core pricing and business mix improvements.
Sustainability business EBITDA
-- Growth over 22% in 2025, with baseline sustainability EBITDA at $300 million; projects $700 million incremental sustainability EBITDA by 2027, $235–$255 million expected in 2026 (60% renewable energy, 40% recycling), with volume and automation cited as key drivers.
Renewable natural gas (RNG) facilities
-- Seven new RNG sites commissioned in 2025; 60% of 2026 RNG volumes are pre-contracted, with remaining volumes expected to clear the voluntary market at $24.50 per MMBtu and RIN pricing anticipated between $2.30–$2.40.
Recycling commodity prices
-- 2025 exit at $62 per ton; 2026 guidance assumes $60–$65 per ton in 1H, ramping to $70 per ton in 2H.
Labor metrics
-- Driver turnover hit a low of 15.7% in Q4, reflecting improved frontline retention and labor cost structure.
Synergy capture (Healthcare Solutions)
-- Achieved above the upper end of $80 million–$100 million SG&A synergy target in 2025; confident in $300 million total synergy target, including $50 million in cross-selling.
Capital allocation outlook
-- Maintenance capex to remain near 10% of revenue long term; tuck-in M&A planned at $100 million–$200 million per year.
SUMMARY
Waste Management

(
WM

+1.65%
)
reported a year characterized by record operating margin, robust cash flow, and significant expansion in its sustainability business despite commodity headwinds. Management emphasized ongoing pricing strength and rapid cost reductions, particularly in labor and SG&A, as key drivers of margin gains and double-digit free cash flow growth. Shareholder returns are set to accelerate in 2026, with a 14.5% dividend increase and a $3 billion repurchase program, returning more than 90% of expected free cash flow. Integration of Healthcare Solutions improved customer metrics above legacy averages, with synergy realization exceeding targets and incremental margin progress projected for 2026 as lost account impact diminishes. Strategic execution in recycling and RNG, despite lower commodity and RIN prices, enabled sustainability EBITDA to grow over 22%, while expansion capex and automation upgrades position the company for further structural returns through 2027.
Approximately $3.5 billion is planned for return to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases in 2026, representing more than 90% of projected free cash flow.
Healthcare Solutions revenue guidance reflects a temporary volume headwind, with lost accounts expected to annualize by the back half of the year and cross-sell momentum anticipated to exceed initial targets.
Connected truck and landfill technology, route automation, and AI contributed to sequenced cost reductions in repair, maintenance, and fleet optimization, supporting operational margins across business lines.
Commodity market normalization remains a sensitivity, with automation and strategic contracting partially insulating recycling and RNG margins from 2025’s sharp price declines.
The leverage ratio closed at 3.1x in 2025, with a clear path to the 2.5x-3x range targeted for 2026, reinforcing balance sheet flexibility for disciplined M&A and future capital returns.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2026 excludes $150 million in accretion expense to align with industry peers and facilitate more direct comparability on operating performance.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
Operating EBITDA
: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, depletion, amortization, and (here) excluding accretion; reflects core profitability of the business excluding non-cash charges and specific non-operating expenses.
RIN (Renewable Identification Number)
: A regulatory compliance credit under the EPA’s Renewable Fuel Standard, integral to pricing and contract strategy in RNG markets.
Accretion Expense
: The expense related to operating landfills, specifically the increase in estimated future landfill closure and post-closure costs; here, restated out of EBITDA guidance for peer comparability.
OCC (Old Corrugated Containers)
: Key fiber commodity price indicator for the recycling segment, sensitive to market demand and supply chain shifts.
Core Price/Core Pricing
: The underlying price increases achieved directly with customers, excluding commodity-related pass-throughs or surcharges, critical for analyzing revenue and margin drivers in collection and disposal.
